prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an outdoor corridor with a raised, sloped snow bank and low retaining wall on the left (0.5 to 5 m away) and a flat sidewalk bordered by trees and a street on the right, receding toward background buildings roughly 25 to 50 m away. Across the five frames, the camera wearer walks forward along the sidewalk while panning left toward the snow bank in frames 2 and 4 and back toward the sidewalk in frames 1, 3, and 5, passing a dog on the left (~1 m away and nearly within arm's reach at the bottom edge of frame 1, and ~1.5 to 2 m away facing sideways/away with its head lowered in frames 2 and 4, out of view in frames 3 and 5). It also tracks a small snow-covered bush on the snow bank as the wearer approaches it from ~2.5 m on the left in frame 3 to ~1–1.5 m on the right in frame 4 and far left in frame 5, while a large tree trunk on the right approaches from ~2.5 m in frame 3 to within arm's reach (~0.5 to 1 m) in frame 5, where it occludes parked cars ~3 to 15 m behind it. Compared to the RGB strip, where uniform white snow washes out surface relief, the depth gradient clearly reveals the step-up of the retaining wall, the slope of the snow bank, and the relative distance between the foreground bush, dog, and mid-ground trees. However, the depth map is unreliable on thin overhead tree branches in frames 2 to 4 (rendering them with inconsistent foreground brightness against the sky), blends the dog's silhouette into the bright foreground ground in frame 1, and flattens background structures beyond ~25 m into uniform darkness.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground objects against a black background as the camera pans left and right along the sidewalk, detecting no objects within immediate arm's reach. In frame 1, it segments two parked cars along the right curb at roughly 3 to 5 m (partially cut off at the right edge) and 12 to 15 m away (separated from each other by ~8 m), while in frame 2 it turns left to segment the dog at ~1.5 to 2 m on the lower left, facing right with its head down and looking away from the camera wearer. In frame 3, as the camera faces down the sidewalk again, it detects the near car (~3 to 4 m on the lower right) and a further car (~10 m ahead, partially occluded by the unsegmented foreground tree trunk), in frame 4 it segments the dog at ~1.5 to 2 m on the lower left facing away and up-slope, and in frame 5 it detects distant parked cars (~12 to 20 m away on the right, partially occluded by the near tree trunk). Compared to the RGB image, the masks help distinguish individual parked vehicles that blend into snowbanks and dark background buildings along the street in frames 1, 3, and 5. However, the map is unreliable in several ways: it completely misses the partly occluded dog at the bottom of frame 1 (~1 m away), misclassifies the dog in frame 4 and a tiny right-edge car fragment in frame 3 as a 'person' even though no other people are present in the scene, and omits all static obstacles such as the tree trunk within arm's reach in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: Because no other people or human hands are visible in the scene, the pose map contains no magenta hand skeletons and renders only two isolated yellow body skeletons across the five-frame strip, with nothing within any other person's arm's reach. In frame 2, a compact, folded yellow skeleton is placed at the bottom-left (~1.5 to 2 m in front of and below the camera wearer) over the dog's body, with the head keypoint cluster oriented down and to the right, facing away from the camera wearer. In frame 3, an upright, elongated yellow torso-and-head skeleton appears near the top-center of the frame, aligned with the vertical leafless tree trunk roughly 2 to 3 m ahead of the camera wearer, while frames 1, 4, and 5 remain completely blank as the dog and trees shift or leave the field of view. Unlike the depth and segmentation maps, the pose map adds no valid spatial detail that is hard to see in the RGB strip. Instead, it is entirely unreliable in this sequence, generating false-positive human skeletal poses on a quadruped dog in frame 2 and on a vertical tree trunk and branches in frame 3.
